subject: Data handling & subprocessors - follow-up (telemetry, residency, logging)
messages:
From: Samantha Moore <s.moore@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Desai <amit.desai@fintechco.com>, security@fintechco.com
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data handling & subprocessors - discovery call follow-up

Thanks for the call this morning — really helpful. A couple quick follow-ups from our security and engineering teams: 

1) Telemetry: Which telemetry vendors (if any) does Redwood share anonymized usage or aggregate metrics with? We need vendor names and the type of data sent.
2) Data residency: We need confirmation that any customer-production data for our workspace will reside only in AWS us-west-2. Is that supported for Dedicated or Private?
3) Logging & retention: What logs do you retain (request/response, metadata, telemetry), for how long by default, and can retention be configured per-account?

If you can share the subprocessor list and a high-level data flow diagram, that would speed our internal review. Happy to loop our security PM into a short call if needed.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Moore
Head of Product Security, FinTechCo
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Moore <s.moore@fintechco.com>
Cc: Amit Desai <amit.desai@fintechco.com>, dev_patel@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data handling & subprocessors - discovery call follow-up

Hi Samantha — great speaking with you and Amit today, appreciate the clear list. See answers inline below and attached: redwood_subprocessors_2027Q1.pdf (full list), redwood_data_flow_diagram.png (high-level), and sso-setup-guide.pdf.

1) Telemetry:
- Vendors: Datadog (metrics/traces), Segment (customer event pipeline for analytics; we use server-side), Sentry (error monitoring), and Mixpanel (product usage aggregation for some PLG flows).
- Data sent: telemetry is limited to non-PII by default; examples: request latency, error types, aggregate token usage, and anonymized IDs. We do not send full request/response payloads to these vendors. The attached subprocessor doc has more detail for each vendor and contractual protections (DPA + SOC 2 attestations where available).

2) Data residency:
- Hosted API: multi-region; default is us-east-1 but we can pin accounts to us-west-2 for enterprise customers on Dedicated or Private deployments.
- Dedicated: yes, we can provision Dedicated capacity in us-west-2 and ensure customer data stays in that region.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): fully customer-controlled; data remains within your VPC/region.

3) Logging & retention:
- We retain operational logs (service metrics, audit trails, request metadata) for 90 days by default. Audit logs (admin actions, config changes) are retained for 365 days by default.
- Request/response payload logs are NOT retained by default for hosted API; for Dedicated we can enable configurable request logging per contract and support custom retention windows.
- Customers can configure retention and opt-out where applicable; retention overrides require a contract amendment for Hosted at enterprise tier.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll send the subprocessor pack (attached) and a short data flow diagram — in progress and attached here.
- Dev (cc’d) can run through telemetry exclusions for any specific endpoints you flag.
- If your security PM wants, we can set a 30-min follow-up this week to go over the subprocessor doc and residency confirmation.

Let me know what times work and if you want Ethan (security) looped in for detailed controls.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Amit Desai <amit.desai@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Samantha Moore <s.moore@fintechco.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data handling & subprocessors - discovery call follow-up

Marissa — thanks for the quick replies and the attachments. A couple of clarifications from our infra team: 

- When you say request/response payload logs are not retained by default for hosted API, does that include model-generated outputs? Our use case sends account PII in prompts for verification flows; we need assurance those payloads are not stored or sent to third parties.
- For telemetry, can Redwood provide a CSV export of the subprocessor list with vendor contact and SOC2 link so our tooling can ingest it?

If you can confirm the above we’ll move ahead with internal signoff for a Dedicated eval in us-west-2.

—Amit
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Amit Desai <amit.desai@fintechco.com>, Samantha Moore <s.moore@fintechco.com>
Cc: ethan_park@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-18T14:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data handling & subprocessors - discovery call follow-up

Amit — thanks, good questions. Quick clarifications: 

- Request/response logs and model outputs: For Hosted API, we do NOT persist customer request or generated outputs as part of our default telemetry or logging. Short-lived operational caches (KV) exist for inference performance but are ephemeral and not written to long-term storage. For Dedicated (customer-dedicated pools) we can disable request logging entirely; for Private deployments data never leaves your environment. We will include specific language for this in the MSA/Security Addendum.

- Subprocessor CSV: attached in the subprocessor PDF is a table; I’ll follow up with a CSV export (redwood_subprocessors_2027Q1.csv) and include vendor contact and SOC2 links. 

Internal note to @ethan_park: can you confirm the standard contract language we propose for Hosted vs Dedicated re: retention/exports and any addendum text specific to telemetry vendors? If there are additional controls (VPC egress restrictions, contract terms) we should surface them to FinTechCo.

If FinTechCo is comfortable with the above, next practical step is scheduling a short security review with Ethan + Dev to confirm Dedicated provisioning timeline for us-west-2. I’m available tomorrow 9–11am PT or Friday 1–4pm PT.

Thanks,
Marissa

----
Attachment stubs:
- redwood_subprocessors_2027Q1.pdf (list of subprocessors, vendor contacts, SOC2 links)
- redwood_data_flow_diagram.png (PNG, 800x600)
